display_name: Get vetting run (read a persisted run by id)
description: Read ONE previously-persisted code-vetting run back by its 'run_id', returning the stored metrics row (including a foreign run's additive target.technology_fingerprint when present) plus the run's structural-metrics and candidate-dead-symbols evidence payloads and the full severity-ranked markdown report. This is the READ side of the suite: it does NOT run any scanner or inference — it looks up a run the inference-backed driver already persisted to the vetting_runs trail (the joseki / scheduled-dogfood path; the bare vet_codebase verb returns inline and does not persist). It exists so the automated AI pass routes its payloads by run_id — a later critic/verify step reads the report + evidence from here instead of carrying a prior step's runtime result forward. Required 'run_id' is the vr-<tag>-<ref>-<stamp> id a prior driver-backed run returned. An unknown run_id is a typed 'run_not_found' refusal (fail-loud, never an empty success); an empty run_id is 'invalid_run_id'. The lookup uses the sanctioned single-namespace state read (no join, no raw SQL) against the plugin's own vetting_runs namespace.
embedding_description: Look up a stored code-vetting run by its run id and return the saved report and metrics: the severity-ranked markdown report, finding counts by severity and dimension, coverage evidence, the structural-metrics distribution, and candidate dead symbols, read back from the persisted trail. For retrieving the results of a run whose id you already hold.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Object: run_id, target ({repo, ref, scope}; a persisted foreign run also has the bounded source_role_partition and technology_fingerprint in the same target JSON), started/finished ISO-8601 timestamps, substrate (heuristic | local_inference | subscription — which engine reviewed/refuted the run), layers_run (L1/L2/L3 executed), files_examined (per-scanner coverage evidence), counts_by_severity (blocker/high/medium/low/advisory), counts_by_dimension, survival_rate (L2->L3 precision proxy; null when nothing was verified), coverage_gaps, allowlist_delta (tracked-debt burn-down snapshot), structural_metrics (per-run complexity/length/params/nesting distribution + worst_offenders[] + the repeated-literal table literals[] — magic-string candidates — plus the named nested-loop pattern class: nested_loops[] each {file, line, language, depth} capped for payload bounds, nested_loops_total (the TRUE count before that cap), nested_loop_languages[] and nested_loop_files_examined (the class's own denominator — it is NARROWER than files_parsed because the detector is language-limited, so an empty nested_loops[] means 'none found in the files examined', never 'none in the target'); null when the structural-metrics scanner did not run), dead_symbols (the candidate-dead-symbols payload: total, by_kind, candidates[] each {file, line, name, kind, confidence, dead_lines} — the 60%-confidence L2-targeting evidence; null when the dead-code scanner did not run), and report (the severity-ranked markdown report text; null for a metrics-only subset run). On an unknown run_id the result is an error, not an empty record.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This is a read-back, not a fresh scan — say so. Lead with the run's headline (target, generated timestamp, severity histogram) and offer the stored markdown report for the finding detail. If the caller wanted a NEW scan, point them at vet_codebase instead. A 'run_not_found' error means no run with that id is in the trail (it may have aged out of the bounded retention, or it was a bare vet_codebase call that did not persist) — not that the code is clean. If target.technology_fingerprint is present, its capability_needs are routing evidence with execution_status 'not_run_by_fingerprint'; do not present them as checks that ran, passed, or found the target clean.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Reading a persisted code-vetting run back from the vetting_runs trail by its run_id.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: run_not_found: no run with the supplied run_id exists in the vetting_runs trail — it was never persisted (a bare vet_codebase verb call returns inline and does not persist; only the inference-backed driver / dogfood path writes a row), or it aged out of the bounded metrics retention. invalid_run_id: the run_id argument was empty or whitespace-only. A RuntimeError about the state_service being unbound means the platform state service is not available to this plugin (a misconfiguration — the read cannot proceed without it).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: run_not_found: confirm the run_id is exactly the value a prior driver-backed run returned; if it was a plain vet_codebase call, its result was returned inline (there is nothing to read back) — re-run through the joseki / dogfood path if a persisted record is needed. invalid_run_id: pass a non-empty run_id. If the state_service is unbound, that is a deployment issue, not a caller error.
